brief: JPM's Sep 15 afternoon briefing frames a second straight equity decline as investors position into Wednesday's FOMC decision, with a sharp oil rally (Saudi cargo cancellation, Libya outages, Russian refinery cut) pressuring rate- and consumer-sensitive stocks while AI-linked names held up better. Restaurants sold off hardest (JP2RST), with long/short positioning at the 0th percentile for the past year and back to 2018, net selling accelerating last week, and no dip-buying in WING or DRI. Commodity open interest hit a record $2.1tn, energy-led. JPM's rates team (Jay Barry) models five Fed Day scenarios ranging from SPX -1.75% (no hike) to +1% (hike plus removing 2025 insurance cuts), judging 'no hike' and 'crush inflation' least likely; Feroli forecasts hikes in both September and December with the dot plot rising to 3.25%. JPM stays Tactically Cautious/Neutral into the Fed, arguing bond-yield volatility, not the yield level, is the bigger equity headwind, even as above-trend growth and >20% EPS growth support stocks. The bank stays bullish on AI/Semis/Mag7, would buy today's AI-pullback dip, and prefers MegaCaps, flagging that the priced 2-hike path could prove too low if energy-driven inflation persists.
